obligations.summary: The Commission shall establish a scientific panel of independent experts by means of an implementing act adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 98(2).

The Commission shall select panel experts based on up-to-date scientific or technical expertise in AI, ensuring independence from providers, ability to act diligently and objectively, and fair gender and geographical representation, in consultation with the Board.

The scientific panel shall advise and support the AI Office in implementing and enforcing the Regulation, particularly regarding general-purpose AI models and systems, including alerting on systemic risks, contributing to evaluation tools, advising on classification, supporting market surveillance authorities, and assisting in the Union safeguard procedure.

Experts on the scientific panel shall perform their tasks with impartiality and objectivity, maintain confidentiality of information, refrain from seeking or taking instructions from anyone, and each shall draw up a publicly available declaration of interests; the AI Office shall establish systems to actively manage and prevent conflicts of interest.

The implementing act establishing the scientific panel shall include provisions on conditions, procedures and detailed arrangements for the panel and its members to issue alerts and request assistance from the AI Office.
